title: High retail inflation : Focus has to be on stabilising prices
description: INDIA’s retail inflation hitting its highest level in two years indicates weakening purchasing power and a squeeze on household budgets. Measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 6.09% last month, inflation has crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper tolerance limit of 6%. After the central bank raised the policy repo rate to 5.5% in October, the Monetary Policy Committee meeting early next month could see another hike. This is likely to keep monthly instalments on loans elevated for a longer period. Food prices, which account for nearly 40% of the price index, continue to be a major contributor. Vegetables, pulses and groceries are costlier, while grains, oilseeds and sugar are seeing simultaneous price pressures. Food inflation accelerated to 8.94% in October.

title: High retail inflation : Focus has to be on stabilising prices
description: INDIA’s retail inflation hitting its highest level in two years indicates weakening purchasing power and a squeeze on household budgets. Measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 6.09% last month, inflation has crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper tolerance limit of 6%. After the central bank raised the policy repo rate to 5.5% in October, the Monetary Policy Committee meeting early next month could see another hike. This is likely to keep monthly instalments on loans elevated for a longer period. Food prices, which account for nearly 40% of the price index, continue to be a major contributor. Vegetables, pulses and groceries are costlier, while grains, oilseeds and sugar are seeing simultaneous price pressures. Food inflation accelerated to 8.94% in October.
